skill.name: kubernetes-architect
skill.description: Kubernetes architecture guidance for cloud-native platforms, GitOps delivery, managed clusters, service mesh, security, observability, multi-tenancy, scaling, and cost optimization.
skill.summary: Design secure Kubernetes platforms with GitOps, observability, resilience, and platform engineering practices.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The only static finding is a false positive. SKILL.md line 37 advises approvals and rollback plans before production changes, which is a safety guardrail rather than reconnaissance or abuse.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid production changes without approvals and rollback plans.

finding_verdicts.reason: The flagged line says to avoid production changes without approvals and rollback plans. This is operational safety guidance, not system reconnaissance or malicious behavior.

content.value_statement: Kubernetes platforms are difficult to design securely across teams, clusters, and cloud providers. This skill guides architecture, GitOps delivery, observability, resilience, and platform engineering decisions.
actual_capabilities: Designs cluster topology, networking, and security boundaries for Kubernetes platforms.
Recommends GitOps workflows using ArgoCD, Flux, progressive delivery, and environment promotion patterns.
Plans service mesh, ingress, network policy, and multi-cluster traffic strategies.
Defines observability stacks with metrics, logs, traces, dashboards, and alerting.
Advises on multi-tenancy, RBAC, quotas, admission controls, and policy as code.
Reviews cost, autoscaling, disaster recovery, backup, and upgrade strategies.
limitations: It provides architecture guidance, not direct cluster administration.
It depends on accurate workload, compliance, and cloud provider details.
It cannot validate live production state without user-provided evidence.
It should not replace formal security, compliance, or reliability review.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Platform
use_cases.description: Design a Kubernetes platform with clear cluster boundaries, GitOps workflows, security controls, and observability from the start.

use_cases.title: Modernize Delivery
use_cases.description: Move from manual deployment steps to declarative GitOps with safer rollouts, environment promotion, and drift detection.

use_cases.title: Harden Shared Clusters
use_cases.description: Improve tenant isolation, RBAC, network policies, admission controls, and operational guardrails for shared Kubernetes environments.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Cluster Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: You need an initial Kubernetes architecture direction.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Kubernetes platform for these workloads: [workloads]. Include cluster topology, networking, storage, security basics, and operating assumptions.

prompt_templates.title: GitOps Rollout Design
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a GitOps deployment model for [team or product]. Compare ArgoCD and Flux, then recommend repository structure and promotion flow.

prompt_templates.title: Multi-Tenant Hardening Review
prompt_templates.scenario: You manage shared clusters for multiple teams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Kubernetes multi-tenancy model: [current model]. Identify risks in namespaces, RBAC, quotas, policies, and network segmentation.

prompt_templates.title: Enterprise Platform Blueprint
prompt_templates.scenario: You need a complete platform architecture.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an enterprise Kubernetes platform for [organization]. Cover multi-cluster strategy, GitOps, service mesh, observability, security, disaster recovery, and cost controls.

output_examples.input: Design a Kubernetes platform for a financial services team using EKS and GitOps.
output: A recommended multi-account EKS topology with separate platform, staging, and production boundaries.
A GitOps model using environment repositories, signed changes, policy checks, and progressive rollout gates.
Security controls covering RBAC, network policy, secrets, image signing, admission control, and audit logging.

output_examples.input: Improve reliability and cost for an existing multi-team Kubernetes cluster.
output: A prioritized review of autoscaling, resource requests, disruption budgets, node pools, and workload placement.
Observability improvements for service health, saturation, error rates, logs, and traces.
Cost actions using right-sizing, spot capacity where appropriate, quotas, and allocation reporting.

output_examples.input: Plan progressive delivery for microservices with service mesh traffic control.
output: A rollout strategy using canary or blue-green releases with measurable promotion criteria.
Traffic splitting guidance across ingress, service mesh, and application-level health checks.
Rollback planning with monitoring signals, release ownership, and approval points.

best_practices: Provide workload scale, compliance needs, cloud provider, and operational constraints before asking for architecture decisions.
Ask for tradeoffs between managed services, self-managed components, and team operating capacity.
Validate recommendations in staging before applying policy, networking, or rollout changes to production.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for production changes without approvals, rollback plans, and current-state evidence.
Do not treat one cluster design as correct for every workload or regulatory context.
Do not skip tenant isolation, resource governance, and observability when standardizing developer platforms.

faq.question: What does this skill help design?
faq.answer: It helps design Kubernetes platforms, GitOps workflows, service mesh patterns, security controls, observability, scaling, and disaster recovery.

faq.question: Does it support managed Kubernetes services?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill covers EKS, AKS, GKE, OpenShift, Rancher, Tanzu, and self-managed Kubernetes patterns.

faq.question: Can it create production-ready manifests?
faq.answer: It can recommend manifest structure and policy direction, but users should test and review all production changes.

faq.question: Is this useful for GitOps migration?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare ArgoCD and Flux, plan repositories, define promotions, and add drift detection.

faq.question: Can security teams use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers RBAC, network policies, Pod Security Standards, admission control, supply chain controls, and compliance patterns.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
